book_title: Chapter 3: The Plumbing Behind Every ₹100 of Revenue
question: How does Protean reach citizens and enterprises across India, and where does every ₹100 of FY26 revenue go between processing costs, salaries, capex, and free cash flow?

epigraph.quote: Collection days rose from 64 to 93 on project receivables as turnkey RFP billings scaled.
epigraph.author: Q2 FY27 Operational Disclosures

web_blocks.title: Hybrid Distribution: Physical Facilitation Meets Enterprise APIs

web_blocks.html: Protean's sales reach blends a wide physical network with direct digital APIs. In Tax Services, it uses 166,000 to 4.42 lakh PAN/TIN centers across 18,000 towns [10, 17]. It pays print, postage, and agent fees—booked as Processing Charges—to local partners [10, 17]. In Pension Services, banks, company HR teams, and Points of Presence (PoPs) bring in users. Protean sits behind them as the central ledger. Under the new UIDAI deal, however, Protean is moving from partner outlets to company-run centers. It is opening 190 District Aadhaar Seva Kendras, with 75 live by July 2026 [13, 16]. These centers need direct leases, biometric gear, and full-time staff [13, 16].

On the corporate side, Protean serves over 1,500 BFSI and business clients via direct APIs [10]. By contrast, state projects like CKYCRR 2.0, Bima Sugam, and AgriStack follow milestone billing rules [10]. This split creates two very different cash cycles. Retail PAN and API clients pay upfront or within 30 days. State project deals pushed debtor days from 63 days in FY25 to 75 days in FY26, and then to 93 days in Q2 FY27 [1, 17].

Processing Charges remain Protean's largest cost item [20]. In FY26, those partner, print, and post fees took ₹493 crore, or 49.4% of revenue [20]. Staff costs added another ₹265 crore, or 26.6% of sales [20]. Moving into company-run UIDAI centers swaps partner commissions for fixed rent and payroll [16]. That trade raises operating leverage when footfall is high, yet hurts margins during slow ramp-up quarters.

web_blocks.title: FY26 Audited Unit Economics: Per-₹100 Revenue Waterfall

web_blocks.html: We trace ₹998 crore of FY26 sales down to ₹12 crore of free cash flow [1, 20]. That path shows why sales growth has not yet built compounding owner cash [1, 20]. Processing fees and staff pay take roughly 76% of every rupee earned [1, 20]. That leaves an operating EBITDA margin of just 11.6% before other income [1, 20].

web_blocks.caption: Protean eGov FY26 Consolidated Unit Economics Waterfall (₹ Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: Out of ₹998 Cr FY26 revenue, operating profit (EBITDA) was ₹116 Cr (11.6%); treasury other income (₹68 Cr) supplied over half of PBT (₹130 Cr), while ₹66 Cr of capex reduced Free Cash Flow to ₹12 Cr.

web_blocks.title: The Capex & Depreciation Squeeze in H1 FY27
paragraphs: In FY26, depreciation jumped 68% YoY to ₹47 crore [1, 17]. It reached ₹62 crore on a TTM basis by September 2026 as Protean capitalized platforms and ASK gear [1, 17].

Tangible assets more than doubled in six months from ₹63 crore in March 2026 to ₹150 crore in September 2026 [15, 16]. That surge squeezed H1 FY27 free cash flow even as sales rose 13.1% YoY [15, 16].

book_paragraphs: Most investors assume a digital public infrastructure company enjoys pure software economics—eighty percent gross margins and effortless cash conversion. One look at Protean's supply chain and FY26 cost waterfall dispels that myth immediately. Protean is not a pure-play software vendor; it is a hybrid transaction-processing utility whose largest cost line is physical and partner fulfillment.

Follow ₹100 of Protean's FY26 revenue through the income statement. Out of ₹998 crore in consolidated sales, roughly ₹493 crore went straight out the door as processing charges, card printing, postage, and facilitation-center commissions. Another ₹265 crore paid employee salaries, and ₹124 crore covered technology hosting, branding, and administrative expenses. That left just ₹116 crore—or ₹11.60 per ₹100 of sales—in core operating profit before depreciation.

Once you deduct ₹47 crore in depreciation and ₹7 crore in finance costs, core operating profit before tax was only ₹62 crore. The only reason Protean reported ₹130 crore in pre-tax profit and ₹101 crore in net profit is that its ₹800-plus crore cash pile earned ₹68 crore in treasury other income—more than half of its entire pre-tax earnings. Even more telling is the cash flow statement: operating cash flow fell to ₹78 crore in FY26 as receivables lengthened to 75 days, and ₹66 crore of capital expenditure on technology upgrades and Aadhaar Seva Kendra rollouts left just ₹12 crore in true free cash flow.

Distribution is the hidden reason for this capital intensity shift. Legacy PAN cards relied on hundreds of thousands of independent facilitation centers that funded their own rent and staff. Under the new ₹1,160 crore UIDAI contract, Protean itself is building and staffing 190 district-level Aadhaar Seva Kendras across 24 states. Tangible assets on the balance sheet jumped from ₹63 crore in March 2026 to ₹150 crore by September 2026, while quarterly depreciation climbed 86 percent year-on-year. Until all 190 centers hit steady-state citizen footfall in late FY27, the company is absorbing fixed overhead ahead of recurring revenue.

Supply-chain procurement also introduces hardware inflation risk that pure software firms never face. In Q1 FY27, management noted that geopolitical tensions pushed up procurement costs for biometric and IT hardware needed across the new centers. Because UIDAI pays a fixed per-transaction fee rather than cost-plus reimbursement, Protean absorbs any hardware price spikes or leasehold delays directly in its operating margin.

Trace that ₹100 revenue waterfall one more time because it holds the key to Protean's cash-flow story. Out of every ₹100 that enters the door, employee expenses and processing/system charges consume roughly ₹89 before depreciation, leaving only ₹11 of core operating profit. Only because Protean earns ₹7 of treasury other income per ₹100 of revenue does pre-tax profit reach ₹13.

Even more telling is what happens below the profit line. In FY26, working-capital absorption—driven by rising government and institutional receivables—and ₹66 Cr of capital expenditure meant that out of ₹100 of revenue, barely ₹1.20 survived as genuine Free Cash Flow. A business that converts 1.2% of sales into free cash flow cannot fund rapid organic compounding without eating into its treasury cushion.

Working-capital discipline is the silent test of any B2G platform. Retail PAN applicants pay upfront before processing begins, creating negative working capital, whereas institutional and central-government turnkey contracts bill on milestone sign-offs that can sit in receivables for months. As Protean's revenue mix shifts toward turnkey DPI projects, watching quarterly debtor days becomes just as important as watching headline sales growth.
Now that we have traced how a single ₹100 revenue bill turns into ₹1.20 of free cash flow, we can ask how durable Protean's competitive moat really is against private rivals.

book_callouts.title: Treasury Income Masks Operating Fragility
book_callouts.text: When interest and mutual fund gains on idle cash contribute more than half of pre-tax profit, the operating business is earning far less than the headline bottom line suggests. Always judge Protean on core operating profit ex-other-income and free cash flow after capex.

book_subsections.title: Why Working Capital Splits Into Two Worlds
paragraphs: Protean's balance sheet runs two clocks at once. When a citizen pays for a PAN card or a fintech buys an e-KYC bundle, cash arrives upfront or within weeks. When a state agency or sovereign registry signs a turnkey RFP for CKYCRR 2.0 or Bima Sugam, billing depends on milestone sign-offs, pushing receivable days from 63 in FY25 to 93 by Q2 FY27.

As New Businesses grow from 10 percent toward management's 25 percent target, owners must watch whether debtor days keep creeping higher—because growth that locks up cash in government receivables destroys return on capital.

book_subsections.title: Operating Scale vs. Fixed Center Overhead
paragraphs: Management's core argument for margin recovery in late FY27 rests on operating scale across the 190 Aadhaar Seva Kendras. Once rent, biometric kits, and center staff are in place, every incremental citizen walk-in drops straight to operating profit. That math works—provided citizen footfall reaches bid assumptions and UIDAI payments arrive on schedule.
